summary: An April 1st humorous RFC offering guidelines for identification and security at IETF meetings, with special attention paid to a sub-group it calls "facial hairius extremis". It is a joke.

eli5.summary: A silly rulebook for checking who is who at a conference, especially people with lots of facial hair. It is just for laughs.

subtitle: A humorous look at identification problems at IETF meetings.

tldr.problem: A disproportionately high percentage of male attendees at IETF conferences have facial hair, leading to frequent cases of mistaken identity.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC proposes practical solutions for both those seeking someone and those being sought: people should ask before making assumptions, and those with facial hair should signal clearly whether they are or are not the person being sought.
tldr.outcome: This April 1st joke highlights a real social problem at conferences and offers lighthearted advice for managing it.

today: RFC 2323 is an Informational RFC published on 1 April 1998, and it is treated as a joke. It remains unobsoleted and serves as a playful commentary on a genuine social phenomenon at conferences.

sections.title: Identification at IETF
sections.content: This April 1st joke document identifies a genuine phenomenon at IETF conferences: an unusually high concentration of male attendees with facial hair. The RFC notes that about 60 percent of IETF men have long-term facial hair, compared to around 20 percent in the general population. When people meet and try to identify each other by physical description, facial hair becomes a frequently mentioned feature, leading to confusion.
sections.eli5: Many people at IETF have beards. When someone says, 'Find the man with a beard', there is a problem: there are lots of them.

sections.title: The Problem: Mistaken Identity
sections.content: Facial hair is one of the most noticeable characteristics used to identify people. Ordinarily this would not be a problem, but at IETF the prevalence of facial hair among men is exceptionally high. The RFC recounts anecdotes of well-known researchers being repeatedly mistaken for each other and receptionists who, when asked to find 'an older Caucasian man with a beard', reportedly blurted out, 'they all have beards!!!!'
sections.eli5: When someone calls out 'Hi John!' and you are actually Scott, that is frustrating. At IETF, this happens a lot because beards are so common.

sections.title: Solutions: Recognition and Signals
sections.content: The RFC proposes practical measures. People seeking someone should pause before assuming identity based on facial hair; they should recognize men as individuals and ask for a name before continuing. Those with facial hair, in turn, should give clear signals: politely correct someone who is mistaken, and if hailed from across a room, use hand signals to confirm or deny they are the person being sought. These simple steps acknowledge facial hair as recognizable but not definitive.
sections.eli5: If you think you see your friend, ask their name first. And if someone yells your name and it is wrong, wave your arm to say no or wave back to say yes.
